title: The three new router POST arms (take-over / correct / substitute) have no router-level or session-level test — all action tests bypass require_session and arm matching
evidence: grep of server/test for the new arm paths: zero router.handle_request hits (the only router-level tests in the file are the wrong-person SSR routes at :1135/:1439/:1764). take_over_and_substitute_http_happy_paths_test and row_actions_authz_negatives_test call actions_handler.handle_* directly with test_db.test_landlord — require_session, CSRF and the arm pattern match are never exercised. The codebase pattern elsewhere (application_integration_test.gleam:822, gdpr:2069, payment:2492) drives API routes through router.handle_request.
detail: A regression that dropped an arm, misordered the match list, or unguarded the session wrapping would ship green (the client URL pins in reference_checks_api_test and bug-hunt would be the only tripwires). P3 — handler-level HTTP simulation plus byte-exact URL pins cover most of the risk.
recommended_fix: Add one router-level test per arm (or one combined): POST through router.handle_request with a session cookie -> 200; unauthenticated POST -> 401/redirect; extend the pattern used by application/gdpr integration tests.
